subject: Day 26: post-visit follow-through; first cooing sounds
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 26. If the 1-month visit was earlier this week, follow through on what the pediatrician flagged. Vowel sounds (ah, ooh) are emerging during awake-alert windows.

Action items
- Act on anything the pediatrician flagged at the 1-month visit (latch correction, supplementation pattern, vitamin D dosing). AAP HealthyChildren on vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Confirm vitamin D 400 IU/day is in place if breastfeeding exclusively or predominantly. AAP HealthyChildren on vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Schedule the 2-month well visit if it is not already booked (target day 56-70). AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- If returning to work soon, confirm the daycare or nanny start date matches the return date with a 1-2 week buffer. ChildCare.gov directory: https://www.childcare.gov/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] First vowel coos (ah, ooh) and quieting to a familiar voice; sustained eye contact during feeds.
- [low concern] Hiccups during or after feeds; wet sneezing; quiet startle to loud sounds.
- [monitor] Forceful arching during or after feeds, or painful spit-up despite hunger cues — possible reflux or cow's-milk-protein intolerance; note it for the next visit.
- [call within 24h] Bloody-mucus stool, or persistent inability to console paired with back-arching during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Take conversational turns with every coo — respond as if he spoke, pause, then answer his next sound. Turn-taking, not raw word count, predicts later language scores. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Sing live during diaper changes; vary it day to day — a lullaby, then something rhythmic. Participation, not pitch, is the active ingredient. Gerry, Unrau, Trainor, Dev Sci 2012: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Tummy time near 20 minutes a day; the football hold across your forearm is a useful variation when floor time stalls. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Wear him in a carrier for a short walk outside during a calm window; keep his chin off his chest and his face visible.

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window (if not yet done).
- Day 35-42: peak-crying curve.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; first round of vaccines.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
